error_message: Hook timed out in 20000ms. | Test timed out in 5000ms.
root_cause: No concurrency limits in Vitest configs cause resource exhaustion when running all six projects in parallel — multiple concurrent embedded Postgres initializations and git subprocess spawnings exceed hook and test timeouts.
trigger: Running pnpm test:run with all six Vitest projects simultaneously and no maxWorkers cap
approach: Add maxWorkers, testTimeout, and hookTimeout to the three affected Vitest configs to cap concurrency and give expensive setup operations sufficient time
prevention_details: Per-package Vitest config now caps maxWorkers (1 or 2) so the scheduler cannot overwhelm the host with concurrent embedded-Postgres probes, DB startups, and git subprocess spawning
commit_message: fix(test-config): cap Vitest workers and timeouts to prevent embedded-Postgres and git-op timeout failures
follow_ups: Consider a shared embedded-Postgres fixture that is started once per worker process rather than per test/suite;Monitor CI wall-clock time to ensure serializing workers does not unacceptably slow the pipeline

error_message: Hook timed out in 20000ms. | Test timed out in 15000ms. | Test timed out in 60000ms.
root_cause: All failing tests have explicit per-test/per-hook timeout overrides (15 s or 20 s) that are shorter than the time needed to run startEmbeddedPostgresTestDatabase() + applyPendingMigrations() (56 migrations) under parallel load, or to run provision-worktree.sh with pnpm install.
trigger: Running the full pnpm test:run suite in parallel — 14+ embedded-Postgres instances compete for system resources, consistently exceeding the hardcoded 20 s budget.
approach: Raise all hardcoded embedded-Postgres and provision-script test/hook timeouts from 15_000/20_000 to 60_000 (and the e2e test to 120_000); raise server and db vitest config ceilings to 60_000
prevention_details: Added JSDoc + runtime console.warn to startEmbeddedPostgresTestDatabase when startup exceeds 30 s so future migration growth is caught before timeouts are exceeded
commit_message: fix(test-timeouts): raise embedded-postgres and provision test timeouts from 20s to 60s
follow_ups: Consider a shared embedded-Postgres fixture started once per worker rather than per suite to reduce total startup time;Monitor CI wall-clock time after this change

error_message: TS6053: File 'server/src/types/express.d.ts' not found | TS2339: Property 'actor' does not exist on type 'Request<{}, any, any, ParsedQs, Record<string, any>>'
root_cause: The triple-slash reference in index.ts pointed to types/express.d.ts but the file was never committed to the repository, causing TypeScript to fail resolving the Express Request augmentation for the actor property.
trigger: Any pnpm typecheck run in CI verify workflow
approach: Create the missing Express Request type augmentation declaring Actor interface with all actor shapes (none, board, agent)
prevention_details: CI typecheck workflow already enforces presence; file now committed so deletion would immediately fail CI
commit_message: fix(server): add missing Express Request type augmentation for actor
follow_ups: Refactor Actor to a discriminated union type with proper narrowing guards;Add CI step to verify triple-slash references resolve

error_message: this release step must run from branch master, but current branch is main.
root_cause: require_on_master_branch hardcoded "master" as the required branch name but the repository's default branch is "main", so every canary release in CI was immediately rejected even though CI was on the correct branch.
trigger: Running ./scripts/release.sh canary from the main branch in CI
approach: Rename function to require_on_main_branch and change the branch comparison target from "master" to "main"
prevention_details: Renamed the function from require_on_master_branch to require_on_main_branch so any future caller using the old name gets an immediate shell "function not found" error rather than a silent wrong-branch rejection
commit_message: fix(release): update branch guard from master to main
follow_ups: Add a shellcheck CI step to catch stale branch-name literals proactively;Audit other scripts for remaining master references that should be main

root_cause: SC2155: combining local/export with command substitution masks subcommand exit codes; SC2034: variables assigned but never read
trigger: CI runs shellcheck on all *.sh files and exits 123 when warnings are present
approach: Split combined local/export+assign into two statements; add :? guard on REPO_ROOT; remove unused variables (cleanup_on_exit in release.sh, worktree_config_path/worktree_env_path in provision-worktree.sh)
prevention_details: ShellCheck CI gate already in place; fixes make the codebase clean so the gate blocks future regressions
follow_ups: Add shellcheck to dev toolchain so developers get feedback before pushing
